synthesis:
UPDATE (this pull, 2026-09-23, reflecting sessions through Wednesday Sept 23 - note: Tuesday Sept 22 is missing entirely from the free Yahoo history endpoint this dashboard's index and universe data comes from, both for the headline indices and the ~1,300-name equity universe; this was confirmed via search to be a genuine data gap, not a market holiday - Sept 22, 2026 was an ordinary Tuesday trading session per multiple outlets' live market coverage, so figures described as a single 'day move' below actually span two real sessions, Tue Sept 22 and Wed Sept 23, compressed together by the gap): Markets gave back a chunk of last week's rally over these two sessions, and the story is a direct continuation/intensification of the rates-and-inflation throughline running since the Sept 16 FOMC hike, not a new independent shock. Tuesday Sept 22 was mixed - the Nasdaq notched a second straight record close (+0.4%) as Meta's Muse-driven chip-sector optimism carried over and oil initially fell ~3% on an Iranian signal it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if U.S. military pressure eased, while the Dow slipped 0.3% and Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin warned 'supply shocks aren't proving short-lived' (a hawkish signal) and oil pared its drop back after President Trump told the UN a U.S.-Iran deal wouldn't come before the November midterms. Wednesday Sept 23 reversed hard across the board: the 10-year Treasury yield surged to roughly 5.11%-5.14% - the highest since July 2007 - after Fed Governor Michael Barr said 'further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion,' and a much-hotter-than-expected S&P Global composite PMI (58.4 vs. 55.3 forecast) reinforced the inflation picture, pushing market-implied odds of an October hike to roughly 66-74%. All three major indices fell Wednesday (Dow -0.7%, S&P 500 -0.8%, Nasdaq -1.1%), with the Russell 2000 leading declines (-1.77% Wednesday alone) on its usual higher rate sensitivity, and breadth was lopsided across this dashboard's filtered universe (495 advancers vs. 799 decliners). No single new dominant catalyst beyond the yield/Fed-hawkishness combination - this reads as profit-taking and rate repricing after last week's rally, not a fresh shock requiring a rewrite of the underlying framing below.

UPDATE (this pull, 2026-09-17): The catalyst this file was waiting on has now happened. The FOMC voted 12-0 on Sept 16 to hike the fed funds rate 25bp to 3.75%-4% — the first hike since 2023 — citing inflation still 'elevated' even as growth stays solid; the statement gave no explicit signal on further moves, but the Fed's own dot plot points to at least one more 2026 hike, and markets are now pricing a second. The 10-year yield pushed through 5% on the decision (5.02% intraday) as Chair Warsh's press-conference remarks doubled down on inflation risk. Equities fell into the announcement and stayed down: the Dow lost 631pts (-1.21%) to 51,461.90, the S&P 500 slipped 0.45% to 7,551.81, and bank stocks had their worst day since February (KBE -2.6%) on fears the hiking cycle isn't over. Oil has pushed above $100/bbl on the still-live Middle East supply story. None of this overturns last pull's framing — it's the resolution of the exact mechanism already described below — so the original synthesis is kept intact underneath rather than rewritten. Markets this week are being driven by one interlocking story: a hotter-than-expected core CPI print (+0.3% m/m) pushed the market-implied odds of a Fed rate hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC from roughly 70% to 90%, sending the 10-year Treasury yield up 12bp to 4.95% — its highest level since 2023 and closing in on 2007 highs. Middle East tensions, including Iran's attacks on commercial and U.S. Navy vessels, are compounding the inflation picture by pushing WTI crude up 3.2% to $97. Credit markets aren't stressed — both IG and HY spreads tightened slightly on the week — and the VIX term structure remains in contango, meaning options markets aren't pricing panic despite small-caps (Russell 2000, -2.2% over 5 days) and the Dow (-2.1%) underperforming a Nasdaq held up by AI-infrastructure capex names. The FOMC decision on Sept 16 is the next clear catalyst for all of the above.

UPDATE (this pull, 2026-09-22): The post-FOMC selloff reversed hard by Monday, Sept 21. The S&P 500 rose 1.49% and the Nasdaq 2.26% (a fresh record-high close, first since June) as the 10-year yield fell back under 5% and WTI crude eased from the prior week's highs - unwinding the exact two headwinds (yields, oil) that drove the Sept 16 hike-day selloff above. A chip-sector rally, sparked Sept 18 when Meta's new consumer AI agent Muse topped Apple's App Store (read as bullish for CPU-side AI-inference demand: Arm +13%, Intel +12%, AMD +9% that session), carried through the weekend into Monday, when AMD crossed a $1T market cap for the first time. Bitcoin's surge past $85,000 the same day lifted Coinbase, Robinhood, and crypto-miner stocks. None of this reverses the FOMC decision itself (still the first hike since 2023, still a hawkish dot plot) - it's markets re-pricing the odds of a second 2026 hike lower after the initial shock, not a change in the Fed's stated path.
